title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: A is a Dedekind domain with fraction field K. Grothendieck works with A-linear additive categories C, called 'Dieudonné categories' over A, that are equivalent to P(O). Here O = End(X) for some object X, and P(O) is the category of right O-modules that are locally free (projective) of finite rank. O is an A-order in a finite-dimensional K-algebra. The previous page proved Morita theory: P(O) and P(O') are A-linearly equivalent iff there is an O-O' bimodule L that is projective of rank 1 on each side. Two maximal orders in the same K-algebra are linked by such an L, and the class of maximal orders is stable under this equivalence.

First paragraph of this page. Maximality is a local condition, and O, O' are locally isomorphic, so the property passes across the equivalence. Hence equivalence classes of A-irreducible 'strictly Dieudonné' categories match Morita classes of maximal orders in central simple K-algebras. Through the generic fibre, these match Br(K). (The text says 'iso classes of Azumaya algebras over A', which is not quite right; see errors.)

Second part: the 2-group of self-equivalences. For two Dieudonné categories C, C', let Équiv(C,C') be the category of A-linear equivalences. When it is non-empty, it is a (bi)torsor category under the monoidal groupoid Équiv(C,C) of autoequivalences.
- Fix X in C. An A-linear equivalence φ is determined up to unique isomorphism by X' = φ(X) together with the ring isomorphism φ_X: O = End(X) → O' = End(X').
- So Équiv(C,C') is the category of pairs (X', u), with u: O ≅ End(X').
- Taking C = C' = P(O), this becomes the category of O-bimodules P that are invertible, i.e. projective of rank 1 for both structures.
- Composition of functors corresponds to tensor product of bimodules.
- Automorphisms of the identity functor are the units of the centre O^♮ of O. In the strict Dieudonné case (centre A) these are A^*. Endomorphisms of the identity functor are the elements of the centre.

The next page packages this as a Gr-category (2-group):
- π_0 = Brd(O), the 'Brandt group' of bi-invertible bimodules, i.e. Bass/Fröhlich's noncommutative Picard group Pic(O);
- π_1 = Z(O)^*, with trivial action;
- a canonical k-invariant ξ ∈ H^3(Brd(O), Z(O)^*).
These categories assemble into a 2-groupoid equivalent to that of orders with invertible bimodules.

Purpose within the 1965 'Galois theory of motives' project: an integral (over a Dedekind base) analogue of describing simple isotypic coefficient categories by Brauer classes. It also describes their automorphism 2-groups, which a gerbe/band-type Galois theory needs. It is an early instance of the Picard 2-group of a ring and its Postnikov (k-)invariant.
errors: The identification with 'classes d'isomorphie d'algèbres d'Azumaya sur A ... i.e. Br(K)' is inaccurate in two ways. First, the classification is up to Morita equivalence (invertible bimodules), not isomorphism. Second, Morita classes of Azumaya A-algebras form Br(A), which is a proper subgroup of Br(K) in general (e.g. Br(Z)=0 but Br(Q)≠0). The correct statement giving Br(K) uses maximal orders in central simple K-algebras, which are in general not Azumaya at ramified primes.
'les éléments de A' for the automorphisms of the identity functor in the strict case should be the units A^* (endomorphisms give A).

The claim that maximality transfers because 'O, O' are locally isomorphic' needs care. Locally, Morita-equivalent orders over a DVR are matrix-type related, not isomorphic. What is true is that over a DVR with complete/henselian or general localization, a Morita equivalence induced by a projective generator preserves maximality. The argument is sketched rather than proved.

ideas.what: Morita equivalence of A-orders via bimodules projective of rank one on both sides; maximal orders in Brauer-equivalent algebras are Morita equivalent, and maximality is Morita-invariant
ideas.modern_name: Morita theory for orders; maximal orders (Auslander–Goldman, Reiner)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Morita (1958), Bass; Auslander–Goldman (1960) for maximal orders; Reiner 'Maximal Orders' (1975)
ideas.where_published: Brauer group material in 'Le groupe de Brauer I–III' (Dix exposés, 1968) uses Azumaya algebras and Morita-type arguments

ideas.what: Morita classes of A-irreducible strictly Dieudonné categories ↔ Br(K) (via maximal orders)
ideas.modern_name: Brauer group via Morita classes of maximal orders / classification of simple A-linear categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: Auslander–Goldman, Brauer group of a commutative ring (1960); classical Brandt/Hasse theory
ideas.where_published: Le groupe de Brauer I (1966/68) treats Br of schemes, not this category-theoretic version

ideas.what: Category of A-linear equivalences C→C' as a torsor under the autoequivalence monoidal category; identified with invertible bimodules, composition = tensor product, Aut(id) = central units
ideas.modern_name: Picard 2-group (Picard groupoid) of a ring; bitorsors under a 2-group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bass (Pic of noncommutative rings, 1968); Fröhlich (1973); Fröhlich–Wall graded monoidal categories (1974); Breen (bitorsors, 1990s)
ideas.where_published: Gr-categories later in Hoàng Xuân Sính's thesis (1975) under Grothendieck; bitorsors in Giraud, Cohomologie non abélienne (1971)

missed.claim: A 1965 dated instance of Grothendieck considering the Picard 2-group of a (maximal) order: invertible bimodules with tensor product and central units as automorphisms of the identity. This came a decade before Sinh's Gr-category thesis that he supervised, and before Bass/Fröhlich's noncommutative Picard group became standard. It is historical priority evidence rather than new mathematics.
missed.quote: on trouve la catégorie des O-bimodules P tels que P est projectif de rg 1 pour les deux structures. La composition des foncteurs correspond au produit tensoriel des bimodules
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents the motivic/arithmetic origin of the Gr-category (2-group) notion in Grothendieck's program, i.e. coefficient categories over Dedekind rings for motives. This is relevant to the history of 2-groups and of integral coefficients for motives.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics (Morita theory of maximal orders, Picard groupoid of bimodules) is classical. Interest lies only in the early date and the motivic context as a precursor of Sinh's Gr-categories; the Br(K)/Azumaya statement is slightly garbled.
transcription_corrections: 'Br(K)': K is written bold/heavy in the image (Br(K)), confirming K = fraction field rather than A.
Final bracket likely reads '[les endom. des foncteurs identiques correspondent aux éléments de O^♮.]' (endomorphisms, with an underlined 'endom.'), not 'autom. ... isomorphes'.
'O^♮*' denotes the units of the centre of O; the next page's 'O^{G*}' is the same symbol O^♮*.
'les élément de A' should be read as the units of A (A^*) mathematically, though the handwriting says 'éléments de A'.
Next-page transcription 'catégories C de Deligne' is almost certainly 'de Dieudonné', matching this page's 'catégories de Dieudonné'.
